minutes.headline: ZBA signaled informal preference for a 120-unit rental plan at Lunenburg Village; hearing continued to May 28.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard a revised concept for 120 rental apartments in five buildings, replacing the approved 64-home plan and the 80-unit modification. After long public comment, mostly from neighbors, members said they favored exploring the rental concept over the 80-unit plan without committing. They asked for full plans, a peer review and school and fiscal impact data, and continued the hearing to May 28.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard a revised concept of rental apartments in five buildings at Lunenburg Village, replacing the approved home plan and the modification.
Members agreed by consensus, with no formal vote, that the applicant should develop the rental plan in detail; the applicant agreed.
The applicant accepted Ross Associates for peer review at the applicant's cost, with plans due at least a week ahead.
The applicant is to provide a fiscal impact study of school-age children and taxes.
Most public comment came from neighbors, raising trees and wildlife, traffic, schools, taxes and property values; the hearing was continued to May 28.

why_it_matters: A rental project in place of single-family homes would change the number of units counted toward the state affordable housing goal, and could affect school enrollment and the tax base, so the fiscal impact study is the document to read.
The board's leaning is informal and no approval has been given, so the plan can still change before any vote.
watch_next: Continued hearing on May 28, with full plans due at least a week ahead.
The applicant's fiscal impact study and the Ross Associates peer review.
